Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB299.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Sanfeng Zang. Fengxue Yanzhao owns the retained root: the founder's mind-seal is shaped like the mechanism of an iron ox — leave, and the seal pins you; stay, and the seal breaks you. And if one neither leaves nor stays — is it sealing, or not sealing? Can anyone say? The elder Luopi came out: I have the iron-ox mechanism — please, master, do not set the seal. Fengxue: used to hooking whales in the vast deep, and now he sighs at frog steps churning the mud and sand. Luopi paused — Fengxue shouted: elder, why not press on? Luopi went to reason it out — Fengxue struck him with the whisk: do you still remember the words? Try to raise them. Luopi went to open his mouth — Fengxue struck him with the whisk again.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi owns the retained raising: back from presenting tea at the provincial office, he raised the whole case — the founder's mind-seal like an iron ox: leave and it pins you, stay and it breaks you; neither leaving nor staying — sealing, or not? The elder Luopi: I have the iron ox, do not seal me. Fengxue: used to hooking whales in the vast deep — now frog steps churning mud. Luopi paused, Fengxue shouted, struck the whisk, twice; the herding lord said: truly the Buddha's teaching and the king's law are one; when the cut is not made at once, the confusion invites itself — and Fengxue stepped down.

Daxiu Zhu owns the retained address: the retreat closed, a monk asked for the going-out sentence — watch your feet. Then the master: leave and the seal pins you, stay and the seal breaks you; to neither leave nor stay — both are at fault. Assembly! how do you get free of this fault? Senses.Explanation: Leave and the seal pins you; stay and the seal breaks you: the iron-ox mind-seal that stamps both moves — raised from the prefecture office to the retreat's closing day. At the root, Fengxue Yanzhao in the Yingzhou prefecture office: the founder's mind-seal is shaped like the mechanism of an iron ox — leave, and the seal pins you; stay, and the seal breaks you. And if one neither leaves nor stays — is it sealing, or not sealing? Can anyone say? The elder Luopi came out: I have the iron-ox mechanism — please, master, do not set the seal. Fengxue: used to hooking whales in the vast deep, and now he sighs at frog steps churning the mud and sand. Luopi paused — Fengxue shouted: elder, why not press on? Luopi went to reason it out — the whisk: do you still remember the words? Try to raise them. He went to open his mouth — the whisk again. Chushi Fanqi, back from presenting tea at the provincial office, raised the case whole — leave and it pins you, stay and it breaks you; neither leaving nor staying — sealing, or not? — the elder Luopi: I have the iron ox, do not seal me — whales hooked in the vast deep, now frog steps churning mud — the pause, the shout, the whisk twice — and the herding lord: truly the Buddha's teaching and the king's law are one; cut not made at once, the confusion invites itself; Fengxue stepped down. Hongzhi Zhengjue's old-case section carries the same case to the same stepping-down, whale-hook verse and double whisk inside. Tianyin Yuanxiu raised it after his Luzu series: the founder's mind-seal like an iron ox — Luopi claimed the ox and asked off the seal — the whale-hook sigh at frog steps treading mud — the shout, the whisk, twice. Feiyin Tongrong, in his running comment on the Linji succession: NanYuan — bare flesh standing a thousand fathews sheer, unproved ones just look; then Fengxue: the seal of the founders and the sages like an iron ox — leave and it pins you, stay and it breaks you — and Feiyin's own verdict behind it: a great tiger wearing a paper hat — it startles you, and it makes you laugh. Daxiu Zhu, closing the retreat: a monk asked for the going-out sentence — watch your feet; then the master: leave and the seal pins you, stay and the seal breaks you; to neither leave nor stay — both are at fault. Assembly! how do you get free of this fault? a long silence — the four quarters up and down with nothing barred, east west south north with no crossing back.
